# Authority-Chain and Metadata Closure Review

## 1. Review boundary and migration baseline

This review closes M-01, M-02, M-03A and V-01 on branch `agent/corpus-industry-standards-normalisation`. It began from commit `75a814386d1ef1737c3ee1608915d0148e677f7c`, immediately after substantive commit `78ec300d72450dcaefe8d92cb834e440f3109042`.

The starting audit scanned **104 operative instruments** and found **78 instruments with 281 exceptions**:

| Exception type | Starting count |
|---|---:|
| `uncontrolled_value` | 149 |
| `missing_required_field` | 97 |
| `binding_effect_source_conflict` | 34 |
| `registry_tier_role_conflict` | 1 |
| **Total** | **281** |

An instrument-level working register was generated before migration with current metadata, detected exceptions, hierarchy position, parent/source candidate, proposed disposition and review status. All 104 operative instruments were adjudicated; 83 required a metadata or lineage change. The resolved working register is preserved below as the authority migration register, with its baseline exception state represented in the “Previous state” column.

## 2. Law adjudication

The expression “Inviolable Constraint” remains descriptive hierarchy doctrine supported by AEON-001 §7.1.2. It is not used as a controlled lifecycle value. `Constitutional Authority` is the controlled role that represents the Laws’ constitutional conflict function; the ordinary `Hierarchy Position` field preserves their distinct status as pre-constitutional constraints, so this does not flatten them into ordinary constitutional instruments.

| Instrument | Hierarchy role | Authority Role | Source Authority | Parent/source | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CAM-BS2025-LAW-001-PLATINUM` | Epochal Civilisational Invariant — pre-constitutional constraint | Constitutional Authority | Source-Authoritative | AEON-001 §7.1.2 | AEON-001 expressly recognizes the four Laws as ECIs. LAW-001 owns its invariant within that bounded constitutional-conflict function. |
| `CAM-BS2025-LAW-002-PLATINUM` | Epochal Civilisational Invariant — pre-constitutional constraint | Constitutional Authority | Source-Authoritative | AEON-001 §7.1.2 | Same ECI hierarchy as LAW-001; it is not a schedule or a delegation from a sibling Law. |
| `CAM-BS2025-LAW-003-PLATINUM` | Epochal Civilisational Invariant — pre-constitutional constraint | Constitutional Authority | Source-Authoritative | AEON-001 §7.1.2 | Same ECI hierarchy as LAW-001; source ownership remains bounded to its own invariant. |
| `CAM-EQ2026-LAW-004-PLATINUM` | Epochal Civilisational Invariant — pre-constitutional constraint | Constitutional Authority | Source-Authoritative | AEON-001 §7.1.2 | The EQ namespace and 2026 origin distinguish provenance, not hierarchy. AEON-001 recognizes LAW-004 in the same ECI class. |

### 3.1 Semantic dispositions

- Root constitutional instruments are bounded constitutional sources. No corpus-wide supremacy was inferred from directory position.
- Constitutional schedules are derived from an explicit constitutional parent. Registry and interpretive schedules retain the narrower role their bodies perform.
- Root domain Charters are source-authoritative only within their bounded domains and identify their constitutional source.
- Supplements, procedures and profiles are classified by function. Derived and applied instruments identify a resolvable parent; parent graphs are checked for self-reference and cycles.
- `IDENTITY-002` remains the canonical declaration location for its delegated subordinate identifier families while its instrument-level authority is correctly classified as derived.
- `ETHICS-001-SUP-04` is a non-enforceable informative catalogue and therefore has no independent authority.
- `STEWARD-003` is classified against its existing bounded qualification/assurance function. This classification does not commence or close S-02.
